A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work with the same title and authors. All 20 pages in each version, including Appendices A–C, were readable; text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original multilabel-classification and label-ranking experiments, including performance tables, convergence curves, and learned log-partition evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix A, including Tables 1–2 and 4–7 and Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: The proposed min-min objectives, jointly learned energy and log-partition models, Algorithm 1, and inference procedures are unchanged. The revised min-max expression concerns the theoretical comparison, not the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same multilabel-classification and label-ranking datasets and scenarios, including the Mediamill convergence experiment in Appendix A.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains exact MLE, generalized Fenchel-Young, MCMC, and min-max comparators; Table 2 retains MCMC and min-max. The corrected min-max formula differs only by constants under the uniform reference used in the experiments, so it does not establish a changed evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, validation and refitting procedures, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and training settings are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same 5000-step, full-batch convergence protocol.

E4.justification: The prior-sample sensitivity experiments in Figures 1 and 3, log-partition generalization checks in Figure 2, and model comparisons in Appendix A are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the experimental results.

E6.justification: All performance entries in Tables 1–2 and 4–7 and plotted results in Figures 1–3 match. No numerical results, rankings, trends, or qualitative experimental findings are added or revised.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the entropy-only min-max expression with a reference-dependent KL(p,q) term and adds an additive constant. Appendix C.4 correspondingly uses LSEg, KL(p,q), and constants throughout Proposition 3's derivation. This is a localized mathematical correction accounting for the general reference measure.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint learning, MLE recovery, MCMC-free optimization, log-partition generalization, and the sparsemax extension.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and the stated limitation concerning sampling from the learned distribution are unchanged. Section 3.3's added explanation that expectations use q rather than p reiterates the fixed-reference sampling rationale already described in Section 3.1.

D1.justification: The JAX implementation disclosure, dataset access information, model details, and optimization settings in Appendix A are unchanged. No new reproducibility or resource information is provided.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the comparison with earlier log-partition optimization approaches in Section 2.7.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 adds 'removing constants,' and Section 3.3 briefly clarifies the gradient-computation explanation. The arXiv version/date annotation is updated; the narrative and section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised equation blocks produce a small local layout adjustment in Section 3.3, including repositioning Proposition 3 and its following text. All figures and tables retain their appearance, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical consistency by restoring the reference-dependent KL term and additive constants in the min-max formulation and its Appendix C.4 proof. The brief explanatory clarifications also help readability. These are limited improvements to the theoretical comparison; the proposed method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
